newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Mideast distillate exports to Asia seen growing.
newsitem.headline: Mideast distillate exports to Asia seen growing.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil firm Pertamina expects Asia to import middle distillates from the Middle East despite rising supplies from regional refiners in South Korea and Singapore, a Pertamina official said on Tuesday.

"Middle distillate demand fluctuations in our region will always create an opportunity for Middle East producers to fill the gap," Hadi Daryono, Pertamina's vice president of corporate affairs, told delegates at an energy conference in Abu Dhabi.

"With the rapid increase in domestic consumption, Indonesia, together with China, are already a large factor in soaking up middle distillate supplies from regional sources such as Singapore and South Korea," he said.

Indonesia's demand for middle distillates -- gas oil (diesel) and jet-kerosene -- was particularly acute during domestic refinery maintenance work or prior to the haj when it had to secure jet fuel for flights to Saudi Arabia.

"As Indonesian and also Asian middle distillate demand continue to grow while the region's supplies become limited, it is most reasonable to expect that additional supplies will have to come from the Middle East," Daryono said.
OPEC member Indonesia is a net importer of refined products mainly in the form of middle distillates.
Mideast refineries primarily export distillates to India, Pakistan and east Africa.

Total net exports of middle distillates from the region are forecast to increase to 1.04 million barrels per day (bpd) in the year 2000 compared to a current 668,000 bpd, according to analysts Seattle Research and Training Centre.
